thought.text: Android Studio has been extracted with the bundled JBR. Next, let's create the marker file that flutter doctor scans (a `.home` pointer inside `~/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio<version>/system/`):

reasoning_content:
Extraction complete. `/opt/android-studio` contains `jbr`, `bin/studio.sh`, and `build.txt`.

The earlier weird tar behavior was probably because my shim was conflicting somehow… no wait, it's fine now. (Probably the earlier failure was due to some quirk of the shim: `tar --no-same-owner -xzf` worked directly. Let me check the shim once more: `#!/bin/sh\nexec /usr/bin/tar --no-same-owner "$@"` — with `tar xzf`, that becomes `--no-same-owner xzf` — that's valid. Weird. Maybe the shim wasn't the one being used at the time… no, actually the error was coming out of /usr/bin/tar, so the shim was being used, but… oh well — it works now. Let me confirm the shim is still working properly with the `tar xz` pattern.)

Next, set up the marker directory:
- `cat /opt/android-studio/build.txt` → "AI-262.xxxxx.x"
- `mkdir -p /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system`
- `echo /opt/android-studio > /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system/.home`
- Test: `/opt/android-studio/jbr/bin/java -version`

Then run flutter doctor -v.

action.command: cat /opt/android-studio/build.txt; /opt/android-studio/jbr/bin/java -version 2>&1 | head -2; V=$(grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' /opt/android-studio/build.txt | head -1); echo "version=$V"; mkdir -p /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio$V/system && echo "/opt/android-studio" > /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio$V/system/.home && cat /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio$V/system/.home
